concept.title: Determining if the file must be referred to Integrity

conbody.p: When a client comes forward to correct previously provided information or provide previously omitted information, the officer determines if the information can be considered an error correction, or if it must be referred to Integrity to be considered under the voluntary disclosure policy.

The voluntary disclosure policy may apply if the client is aware that misinformation resulted in an inappropriate payment of benefits and is attempting to correct this situation. Unless specified otherwise, it is presumed that in providing the information, the client is in agreement that benefits were not payable.

To determine if the new information can be considered an error correction or must be referred to Integrity, the officer refers to Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity . Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity

When the RFS was undisclosed on a previous claim and a potential overpayment (OP) situation exists, the officer refers to Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity to determine if the RFS must be referred to Integrity for investigation. Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity

section.title: Pending the Adjudication Issue (ADJ) WI when the reason for separation (RFS) is referred to Integrity

conbody.p: When the RFS is referred to Integrity, the officer moves the ADJ WI to Pending until the investigation is complete and the case is adjudicated. When the ROD for the Integrity case is created, the ADJ WI for the RFS moves to the officer’s current workload. The officer then completes the ADJ WI by selecting the Decision already on file option.
